tutorial.addition.count_all.title: Putting together
tutorial.addition.count_all.see: Two berries here. One more berry here. Put them together and count them all.
tutorial.addition.count_all.model: Now they sit in the frame together. Touch each one as you count: one, two, three.
tutorial.addition.count_all.worked: Two and one more makes three. The plus sign means put together.
tutorial.addition.count_all.try: One berry, and two more. Count them all. How many?
tutorial.addition.count_on.title: Counting on
tutorial.addition.count_on.see: Four berries here, two there. You could count all six. But you know there are four.
tutorial.addition.count_on.model: So start at four and take two hops: five, six. You never counted the first four again.
tutorial.addition.count_on.worked: Four plus two is six. Start at the bigger number and count on. It is faster every time.
tutorial.addition.count_on.try: Start at five. Take two hops. Where do you land?
tutorial.addition.make_ten.title: Making ten
tutorial.addition.make_ten.see: Seven in the frame. Three empty spaces left. Seven and three fill it exactly.
tutorial.addition.make_ten.model: Three more arrive, and the frame is exactly full. Seven and three are partners: together they make ten.
tutorial.addition.make_ten.worked: Seven plus three is ten. A full frame is always ten. You never count it.
tutorial.addition.make_ten.try: Six are in. Four more arrive. Does the frame fill up?
tutorial.addition.teen_numbers.title: Ten and some more
tutorial.addition.teen_numbers.see: One whole frame, and three more beside it. That is thirteen: a ten and a three.
tutorial.addition.teen_numbers.model: The tall bar is ten. The small squares are ones. Thirteen is one bar, three squares.
tutorial.addition.teen_numbers.worked: Thirteen plus two is fifteen. The ten stays put. You only add to the ones.
tutorial.addition.teen_numbers.try: Eleven, and two more squares. The ten does not change. How many now?
tutorial.addition.bridge_ten.title: Past the next ten
tutorial.addition.bridge_ten.see: Sixteen already, and four more coming. Watch the second frame fill right up.
tutorial.addition.bridge_ten.model: Four hops from sixteen: seventeen, eighteen, nineteen, twenty. You land exactly on the next ten.
tutorial.addition.bridge_ten.worked: Sixteen plus four is twenty. Ask yourself first: how far is it to the next ten?
tutorial.addition.bridge_ten.try: Seventeen, three hops. How far is it to twenty?
tutorial.addition.tens_and_ones.title: Tens and ones
tutorial.addition.tens_and_ones.see: Twenty-two is two bars and two squares. Three more squares arrive. The bars do not move.
tutorial.addition.tens_and_ones.model: The same short walk as two plus three. Just further along the line.
tutorial.addition.tens_and_ones.worked: Twenty-two plus three is twenty-five. Add the ones. The tens stay put.
tutorial.addition.tens_and_ones.try: Thirty-one, five hops along. Where do you land?
tutorial.addition.carrying.title: When the ones fill up
tutorial.addition.carrying.see: Sixty-eight, and five more squares. Only two fit. Then ten squares become a new bar.
tutorial.addition.carrying.model: So take it in two steps. Two hops to seventy, then three more. Seventy is the resting place.
tutorial.addition.carrying.worked: Sixty-eight plus five is seventy-three. Go to the ten first. The rest is easy from there.
tutorial.addition.carrying.try: Seventy-seven and nine. Stop at eighty on the way. Where do you finish?
tutorial.subtraction.take_away.title: Taking away
tutorial.subtraction.take_away.see: Three berries. One gets eaten. It stays drawn, with a cross.
tutorial.subtraction.take_away.model: Taking away is one hop backwards. Three, then back to two.
tutorial.subtraction.take_away.worked: Three take away one is two. The minus sign means something went away.
tutorial.subtraction.take_away.try: Six berries, two eaten. Count the ones with no cross. How many are left?
tutorial.subtraction.count_back.title: Counting back
tutorial.subtraction.count_back.see: Eight berries, three eaten. You can count the five left. There is a quicker way.
tutorial.subtraction.count_back.model: Start at eight and hop back three: seven, six, five. Same answer, less counting.
tutorial.subtraction.count_back.worked: Eight minus three is five. Start at the big number and walk backwards.
tutorial.subtraction.count_back.try: Start at nine. Hop back four. Where do you stop?
tutorial.subtraction.bridge_back.title: Back through ten
tutorial.subtraction.bridge_back.see: Thirteen berries, five eaten. Counting back one at a time is slow.
tutorial.subtraction.bridge_back.model: Stop at ten on the way. Three hops down, then two more.
tutorial.subtraction.bridge_back.worked: Thirteen minus five is eight. Go down to ten first, then take the rest.
tutorial.subtraction.bridge_back.try: Fourteen, six back. Stop at ten on the way. Where do you finish?
tutorial.subtraction.teens_back.title: Taking a big bite
tutorial.subtraction.teens_back.see: Sixteen is a full frame and six more. Take eight away and the second row goes.
tutorial.subtraction.teens_back.model: Six hops bring you to ten. Two more reach eight. Six and two make eight.
tutorial.subtraction.teens_back.worked: Sixteen minus eight is eight. Break the eight at ten.
tutorial.subtraction.teens_back.try: Seventeen, eight back, stopping at ten. Where do you land?
tutorial.subtraction.tens_and_ones.title: Taking from the ones
tutorial.subtraction.tens_and_ones.see: Twenty-four is two bars and four squares. Take three squares. The bars are untouched.
tutorial.subtraction.tens_and_ones.model: Three small hops back. The ten is the same. Only the ones changed.
tutorial.subtraction.tens_and_ones.worke: Twenty-four minus three is twenty-one. Take from the ones. The tens only move if the ones run out.
tutorial.subtraction.tens_and_ones.try: Thirty-eight, five back. Where do you stop?
tutorial.subtraction.borrowing.title: When the ones run out
tutorial.subtraction.borrowing.see: Eighty-four is eight bars and four squares. You need seven, and there are four.
tutorial.subtraction.borrowing.model: Take four to reach eighty. Then break a bar and take three.
tutorial.subtraction.borrowing.worked: Eighty-four minus seven is seventy-seven. Down to the ten first, then the rest.
tutorial.subtraction.borrowing.try: Ninety-four, eight back, stopping at ninety. Where do you finish?
tutorial.counting.to_five.title: Counting things
tutorial.counting.to_five.see: Three berries. Count them out loud. Touch each one once.
tutorial.counting.to_five.model: The frame holds them still. Nothing gets counted twice. The last number is how many.
tutorial.counting.to_five.worked: A full row is five. Soon you will see five without counting.
tutorial.counting.to_five.try: Count these. How many are there?
tutorial.counting.to_ten.title: Five and some more
tutorial.counting.to_ten.see: Five in one group, two in the other. You do not need to start from one.
tutorial.counting.to_ten.model: The top row is five. Count on to seven. Seven is five and two.
tutorial.counting.to_ten.worked: Eight is a full row and three more. Read the rows, do not count.
tutorial.counting.to_ten.try: A full row and some more. How many are there?
tutorial.counting.ten_and_more.title: Past ten
tutorial.counting.ten_and_more.see: One frame is full, so that is ten. Three more sit in the next one.
tutorial.counting.ten_and_more.model: Thirteen is one ten and three ones. That is what the 1 and 3 say.
tutorial.counting.ten_and_more.worked: Do not count a full frame. See ten. Then count what spills over.
tutorial.counting.ten_and_more.try: A full ten and some more. How many altogether?
tutorial.comparison.more_or_less.title: More or fewer
tutorial.comparison.more_or_less.see: Two this side, five that side. You can see which pile is taller.
tutorial.comparison.more_or_less.model: On the number line, the greater number is further along.
tutorial.comparison.more_or_less.worked: Ten is greater than eight. Ten comes later when you count. So eight is fewer.
tutorial.comparison.more_or_less.try: Which pile has fewer? Tap the smaller number.
tutorial.comparison.compare_teens.title: Close numbers
tutorial.comparison.compare_teens.see: Fourteen and thirteen. The piles look almost the same. Looking is not enough now.
tutorial.comparison.compare_teens.model: Put them on the line. Fourteen sits further along than thirteen, so fourteen is greater.
tutorial.comparison.compare_teens.worked: Both start with a ten. When the tens match, the ones decide it.
tutorial.comparison.compare_teens.try: Which number is greater? Tap it.
tutorial.pattern_matching.ab_repeat.see: One, two, one, two. The same two numbers take turns. The shapes show you where.
tutorial.pattern_matching.ab_repeat.mode: Find the part that repeats. Here it is just two long. Then say it again to yourself.
tutorial.pattern_matching.ab_repeat.work: Four, three, four, three, four. After a four comes a three, every single time.
tutorial.pattern_matching.ab_repeat.try: Seven, six, seven, six, seven. What comes next?
tutorial.pattern_matching.longer_core.se: This time three numbers take turns instead of two. Say them once: four, one, six.
tutorial.pattern_matching.longer_core.mo: Four, one, six, and four is back. The numbers start over. So do the shapes.
tutorial.pattern_matching.longer_core.wo: After four and one comes six. Count where you are in the repeat.
tutorial.pattern_matching.longer_core.tr: Two, six, four, two, six. Which one takes its turn next?
tutorial.pattern_matching.tricky_core.se: Nine, twelve, sixteen. Bigger numbers, and uneven gaps. You cannot tell what is next yet.
tutorial.pattern_matching.tricky_core.mo: Now you can. Nine, twelve, sixteen, then nine again: those three are the part that repeats.
tutorial.pattern_matching.tricky_core.wo: After nine and twelve comes sixteen. Just like the first time.
tutorial.pattern_matching.tricky_core.tr: Sixteen, twenty, twelve, sixteen, twenty. What comes next?
tutorial.number_sequence.one_more.title: What comes next
tutorial.number_sequence.one_more.see: One, two, three, four. This is counting. The last number is missing.
tutorial.number_sequence.one_more.model: Each step is one hop forward. The next number is one more.
tutorial.number_sequence.one_more.worked: Three, four, five, six, and then seven. One more, every time.
tutorial.number_sequence.one_more.try: Four, five, six, seven. What number comes next?
tutorial.number_sequence.skip_two.title: Counting in twos
tutorial.number_sequence.skip_two.see: Two, four, six, eight. These jump. The gap is two every time.
tutorial.number_sequence.skip_two.model: On the line each step is two hops, not one. Find the gap first, then take it again.
tutorial.number_sequence.skip_two.worked: Six, eight, ten, twelve, and then fourteen. Two more each time.
tutorial.number_sequence.skip_two.try: Seven, nine, eleven, thirteen. Keep the pattern going.
tutorial.number_sequence.bigger_jumps.se: One, four, seven, ten. Still even jumps, just longer ones.
tutorial.number_sequence.bigger_jumps.mo: Measure one gap and you have them all. Every step is three.
tutorial.number_sequence.bigger_jumps.wo: Three, six, nine, twelve, and then fifteen. Add three to the last one you can see.
tutorial.number_sequence.bigger_jumps.tr: Five, eight, eleven, fourteen. What comes next?
tutorial.multiplication.harder_tables.se: Six boxes of seven. Here knowing beats counting.
tutorial.multiplication.harder_tables.mo: Six sevens are forty-two. Say it once, and you never count it again.
tutorial.multiplication.harder_tables.wo: Seven times eight is fifty-six. This one is worth simply knowing.
tutorial.multiplication.harder_tables.tr: Eight sixes. Lean on six eights if it helps: it is the same fact.
tutorial.multiplication.two_digit.title: Two-digit times
tutorial.multiplication.two_digit.see: Three boxes of twelve is thirty-six. Drawing every berry stops helping around here.
tutorial.multiplication.two_digit.model: Split it. Three tens is thirty. Three twos is six.
tutorial.multiplication.two_digit.worked: Four tens is forty. Four fours is sixteen. Together, fifty-six.
tutorial.multiplication.two_digit.try: Three fourteens. Split it into three tens and three fours.
tutorial.division.sharing.title: Sharing out
tutorial.division.sharing.see: Six berries, two boxes, shared fairly. Three go in each. Nobody gets more than anybody else.
tutorial.division.sharing.model: Three boxes instead of two. Now it is two each. The same six berries.
tutorial.division.sharing.worked: Six shared by two is three. Two threes are six. Sharing undoes grouping.
tutorial.division.sharing.try: Eight berries into two boxes. How many in each?
tutorial.division.harder_tables.title: The harder shares
tutorial.division.harder_tables.see: Forty-two berries in six boxes. Seven in each, and no leftovers.
tutorial.division.harder_tables.model: Forty-two shared by six is seven. Six sevens make forty-two.
tutorial.division.harder_tables.worked: Fifty-six shared by seven is eight. Seven eights are fifty-six.
tutorial.division.harder_tables.try: Forty-eight shared by eight. Which times fact gives you forty-eight?
tutorial.division.two_digit.title: Two-digit shares
tutorial.division.two_digit.see: Forty-two in three boxes. Fourteen in each. Too full to count.
tutorial.division.two_digit.model: Stop counting and ask instead. How many fourteens make forty-two? Three.
tutorial.division.two_digit.worked: Eighty-four shared by fourteen is six. Six fourteens are eighty-four.
tutorial.division.two_digit.try: Ninety-six shared by twelve. How many twelves make ninety-six?
math.hint.rel.how_many_more: You have {known}. How many more to make {total}?
math.hint.rel.count_up: Something and {known} makes {total}. Start at {known} and count up to {total}.
math.hint.rel.other_part: {total} is the whole, and {known} is one part. What is the other part?
tutorial.addition.missing_part.title: The hidden part
tutorial.addition.missing_part.see: Eight altogether. You can see five. The rest are hidden.
tutorial.addition.missing_part.model: Start at five. Count up to eight. Three hops, so three are hidden.
tutorial.addition.missing_part.worked: Five and three make eight. The question mark was three. Counting up finds a part.
tutorial.addition.missing_part.try: Ten altogether, six of them here. Count up from six. How many are hidden?
tutorial.addition.balance.title: Both sides the same
tutorial.addition.balance.see: The same eight, the same five, the same hidden part. Only the writing changes.
tutorial.addition.balance.model: The whole is written first. Eight is five and three. Equals means both sides match.
tutorial.addition.balance.worked: Nine is four and five. Four and five is nine. Both ways are true.
tutorial.addition.balance.try: Nine is four and something. What keeps both sides the same?
tutorial.comparison.compare_larger.title: Longer numbers
tutorial.comparison.compare_larger.see: 44 and 99. Both have two digits. Look at the left digit first.
tutorial.comparison.compare_larger.model: On the line, 99 sits much further along. Greater still means further, however long the number gets.
tutorial.comparison.compare_larger.worke: 142 against 176. The hundreds match, so move right: four tens against seven tens.
tutorial.comparison.compare_larger.try: 512 or 550. Same hundreds. Which tens are greater?
tutorial.number_sequence.big_skips.title: Big skips
tutorial.number_sequence.big_skips.see: 150, 160, 170, 180. Big numbers, but the jump is small.
tutorial.number_sequence.big_skips.model: Measure one gap and you have them all. 180 plus ten is 190. Only the tens digit moves.
tutorial.number_sequence.big_skips.worke: 268, 278, 288, 298, then 308. Ten more each time, straight past the hundred.
tutorial.number_sequence.big_skips.try: 391, 416, 441, 466. Find the gap once, then take it again.
math.hint.rel.how_many_went: You had {start}. Now there are {left}. How many went?
math.hint.rel.how_many_started: Something lost {gone} and {left} were left. How many were there to start?
math.hint.rel.left_after: {left} is what is left when you take some away from {start}. How many were taken?
math.hint.rel.both_sides: This side makes {total}. The other side has {known}, so it needs enough to reach {total} too.
tutorial.subtraction.missing_part.title: What went
tutorial.subtraction.missing_part.see: Twelve to begin with, and only five left. The crossed-out ones are what went. Count them.
tutorial.subtraction.missing_part.model: Count back from twelve to five. Seven hops. Seven is what went.
tutorial.subtraction.missing_part.worked: Twelve take away seven leaves five. The question mark was seven.
tutorial.subtraction.missing_part.try: Ten to begin with, four still there. How many went?
tutorial.subtraction.start_unknown.title: How many at the start
tutorial.subtraction.start_unknown.see: Three went and eight are left. Neither is the answer. The whole bar is.
tutorial.subtraction.start_unknown.model: Count forwards instead. Eight left, plus the three that went. That is the start.
tutorial.subtraction.start_unknown.worke: Eleven take away three leaves eight. So there were eleven to begin with.
tutorial.subtraction.start_unknown.try: Four went and nine are left. Put them back together. How many at the start?
tutorial.subtraction.balance.title: The answer first
tutorial.subtraction.balance.see: Nine, four taken, five left. Ordinary so far. Watch where the five goes.
tutorial.subtraction.balance.model: Five is nine take away four. The answer is written first. Still true.
tutorial.subtraction.balance.worked: Eight is thirteen take away five. Read it from the left: eight is what you get.
tutorial.subtraction.balance.try: Seven is eleven take away something. What has to go in the gap?
tutorial.addition.both_sides.title: Both sides must match
tutorial.addition.both_sides.see: Two towers, same height. That is all the equals sign asks for.
tutorial.addition.both_sides.model: This side makes seven. The other side has five. It needs two more.
tutorial.addition.both_sides.worked: Four and three make seven. The gap must make seven too.
tutorial.addition.both_sides.try: This side makes nine. The other side has six. How many more does it need?
math.hint.rel.each_group_size: {known} groups make {total} altogether. How many in each group?
math.hint.rel.how_many_groups: Groups of {known} make {total} altogether. How many groups?
math.hint.rel.shared_into: {known} shared out gives {total} in each group. How many groups?
math.hint.rel.how_many_shared: Shared into {known} groups it gives {total} each. How many were there to start?
tutorial.multiplication.missing_factor.s: Twelve berries in three boxes, the same in each. You cannot see how many.
tutorial.multiplication.missing_factor.m: Four boxes of three is also twelve. The hidden number depends on how many boxes there are.
tutorial.multiplication.missing_factor.w: Three boxes of four is twelve. The question mark was four.
tutorial.multiplication.missing_factor.t: Two boxes make ten altogether. How many in each box?
tutorial.division.missing_groups.title: How many boxes?
tutorial.division.missing_groups.see: Twelve berries, three in each box. Four boxes, and none left over.
tutorial.division.missing_groups.model: Put four in each box. Then you need three boxes. Same twelve berries.
tutorial.division.missing_groups.worked: Twelve shared three at a time fills four boxes. The question is how many boxes.
tutorial.division.missing_groups.try: Twenty berries, five in each box. How many boxes?
tutorial.division.start_unknown.title: How many to start?
tutorial.division.start_unknown.see: Three boxes with five in each. Fifteen berries went in.
tutorial.division.start_unknown.model: Five boxes of three is the same fifteen. Count the boxes and the share.
tutorial.division.start_unknown.worked: Three boxes gave five each. So fifteen went in. Only the ending is written.
tutorial.division.start_unknown.try: Shared into four boxes it gave three each. How many were there to start?
tutorial.multiplication.equal_groups.see: Two boxes, three berries in each. Equal boxes are what makes this work.
tutorial.multiplication.equal_groups.mod: Three boxes of two is also six. The same berries, shared out a different way.
tutorial.multiplication.equal_groups.wor: Two times three is six. The times sign means groups of.
tutorial.multiplication.equal_groups.try: Two boxes, four in each. How many berries altogether?
tutorial.multiplication.skip_counting.se: Three boxes of ten. Ten, twenty, thirty. You already know this one from counting.
tutorial.multiplication.skip_counting.mo: Fives work the same way. Five, ten, fifteen, twenty: four boxes of five is twenty.
tutorial.multiplication.skip_counting.wo: Four times five is twenty. Counting in fives is faster than counting berries.
tutorial.multiplication.skip_counting.tr: Three tens. How many is that?
tutorial.multiplication.threes_and_fours: Three boxes of four. Threes and fours you have to learn.
Four boxes of three is the same twelve. Turning it round never changes the answer.
Three times seven is twenty-one. Seven, fourteen, twenty-one: three jumps of seven.
Four sevens. Three sevens is twenty-one. Add one more seven.
tutorial.multiplication.zero_and_squares: Three boxes with nothing in them. Three groups of nothing is still nothing.
Four boxes of four. When both numbers match, the answer is a square: sixteen.
Four times four is sixteen. The squares are worth knowing early; the rest lean on them.
Five times zero. Five boxes, nothing in any of them.
tutorial.division.tens_and_fives.title: Sharing tens and fives
tutorial.division.tens_and_fives.see: Twenty berries, five in each box. Four boxes, and nothing left over.
tutorial.division.tens_and_fives.model: Thirty shared ten at a time is three boxes. Tens share as easily as they count.
tutorial.division.tens_and_fives.worked: Twenty shared by five is four. Four fives are twenty.
tutorial.division.tens_and_fives.try: Forty shared by four. How many fours make forty?
tutorial.division.threes_and_fours.title: Sharing threes and fours
tutorial.division.threes_and_fours.see: Twenty-one berries in three boxes. Seven in each, and none spare.
tutorial.division.threes_and_fours.model: Four boxes of six is twenty-four. Every share is a times you know.
tutorial.division.threes_and_fours.worke: Twenty-one shared by three is seven. Three sevens are twenty-one.
tutorial.division.threes_and_fours.try: Twenty-four shared by four. Which four makes twenty-four?
tutorial.division.zero_and_squares.title: Nothing, and equal shares
tutorial.division.zero_and_squares.see: Four boxes with nothing in them. Nothing shared out is still nothing in each.
tutorial.division.zero_and_squares.model: Twenty-five in five boxes. Five in each. The share and the boxes match.
tutorial.division.zero_and_squares.worke: Nothing shared by four is nothing. There is no berry to give anybody.
tutorial.division.zero_and_squares.try: Twenty-five shared by five. How many fives make twenty-five?
